finding_key: packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts::mass-assignment on the v1 patch document route reaches the (now-modified) documentservice.updatedocument with the raw request body
evidence: Verified the cited chain in the supplied files: `ApiV1DocumentsController.update` (documents.controller.ts ~line 79) declares `@Body() body: { title?: string }` — an inline type literal, so `design:paramtypes` is `Object` and Nest's ValidationPipe (`main.ts:59-66`) skips it via `toValidate()`'s native-type exclusion, meaning `whitelist`/`forbidNonWhitelisted` never strip extra keys; the body then flows verbatim into `DocumentService.updateDocument` (`document.service.ts:98-101`), whose new `{ ...data, updatedAt: new Date() }` spread forwards it to `prisma.document.update`, which accepts unchecked scalars such as `workspaceId`, `authorID`, `fileId`, `type`, `createdAt` at runtime. `WorkspaceScopeGuard` plus the preceding `getDocumentOrThrow({ id, workspaceId })` only bind the URL workspace, not a body-supplied one, so a caller can move/plant a document into a workspace they are not a member of, or alias `fileId` to another document's blob (which `document-file.controller.ts` then serves after authorizing on the attacker-controlled document). The contrast with `DocumentController.updateDocument`'s explicit whitelist + second `assertMember` (`document.controller.ts:183-196`) confirms the v1 path is the unguarded sibling; the claim correctly labels it pre-existing but touched by this diff.
